analysis:
Examined both Serve head excerpts, StartupPreload metadata, patch and base source against the indexed threat model and supplied T-041 detail. StartupPreload.swift head lines 304–310 now enqueue memory-skipped, memory-failed and unattempted candidates for recovery, excluding cancelled, shutting-down or explicitly stopped drivers. Serve.swift:497 adds the current recovery task to preload cancellation/waiting; :523 replaces inline slot teardown with unloadAllModelsForShutdown(). No concrete regression is established by these call-site changes.
Relevant integration contracts concern A-018, TB-007/TB-012, T-029, T-059/T-060 and native lifecycle availability: inspect SelectedModelRecovery's selection filtering, retry bounds, idle-unload interaction, serialized memory/slot admission and add-on-hold fencing. The new enqueue guard does not itself check servingDrain.refusing, but whether this permits loading during a hold depends on the recovery implementation; its absence here is not proof of a missing control. Verify unloadAllModelsForShutdown preserves complete teardown and that recovery cannot restart after shutdown cancellation or leave native owners unreachable.
Surrounding Serve.swift:340–358 preserves authenticated cache-scope forwarding (T-041); :416–439 preserves connection-control authorization invalidation (T-053); :589–610 retains fixed process-key and binary/runtime claims with fresh registration evidence. No changed encryption, attestation, credential exposure or billing behavior is visible. The recovery and shutdown-helper implementations are outside this batch, leaving material availability/lifecycle questions for integration rather than supported findings.
